stories.headline: Man United-linked Dominic Calvert-Lewin signs new Leeds contract
stories.summary: Leeds United have announced striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new two-and-a-half-year contract with the club.
stories.body:
Leeds United have announced striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new two-and-a-half-year contract with the club.

The 29-year-old has kick-started his career since leaving Everton as a free agent in 2025 to join Leeds on a three-year deal following their promotion back to the Premier League.

He scored 14 top-flight goals last season and has five in 11 appearances this term, while his form at Elland Road has seen him recalled to the England squad.

The deal comes amid reports that Man United were potentially interested in the striker.

"Leeds United are delighted to announce Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new contract with the club," a statement said.

"The England international has put pen to paper on a two-and-a-half-year deal at Elland Road, keeping him in West Yorkshire until the summer of 2029."

- Football's main character this week: Jude Bellingham is in a new stratosphere

- Man United's costly errors overshadow early progress under Mauricio Pochettino

Large chunks of Calvert-Lewin's nine-year spell at Everton were blighted by injury, but he missed only three league games last season and has started in all 11 top-flight fixtures in the current campaign.

He won the Premier League's Player of the Month Award in December after scoring in six consecutive matches.

After being recalled by England for a 1-1 friendly draw with Uruguay in March, Calvert-Lewin retained his place in Thomas Tuchel's squad for Nations League matches against Spain and Czechia.

His latest England appearance was against Spain earlier this month when he stepped off the bench to win his 15th cap in the Three Lions' 3-2 Nations League win.

Information from PA contributed to this report.

stories.headline: 2026 NFL Thanksgiving preview: Picks, predictions, schedule, odds, fantasy tips
stories.summary: Eagles-Cowboys and Chiefs-Bills are still on deck. We have the top storylines, bold predictions, stats to know, fantasy/betting nuggets and more.
stories.byline: NFL Nation, Pamela Maldonado, Eric Moody, Seth Walder
stories.body:
Holiday football is here, and the NFL started this season's Thanksgiving week slate a day earlier than normal. On Wednesday night, the Rams beat the Packers. But we have three great Thanksgiving Day games, too.

The Lions and Packers kicked it off, and an NFC East showdown between the Eagles and Cowboys is up next. And to conclude Thursday's games, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs will visit Josh Allen and the Bills in the first clash of NFL MVPs on the holiday, per the Elias Sports Bureau.

Ahead of the matchups, our NFL Nation reporters take you inside each locker room with key storylines and a look back at each team's history playing on Thanksgiving. ESPN Research provides optimistic stats for every team, and betting analyst Pamela Maldonado hits betting insights for each contest. Plus, analytics writer Seth Walder makes bold predictions and fantasy analyst Eric Moody shares fantasy football intel. We also have Football Power Index (FPI) game projections, and three analysts -- Maldonado, Moody and Walder -- give us final score picks for the games.

Eagles (3-7) at Cowboys (5-6)
Thursday, 4:30 p.m. ET | Fox | DAL -8.5 (47.5 O/U)

What we're hearing on the Eagles: With edge rusher Jonathan Greenard getting healthier and counterpart Nolan Smith Jr. continuing his surge, the Eagles have racked up 11 sacks and 15 QB hits over the past two games. "I've been telling you guys that it would come, but you didn't believe me," defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said of the pass rush. "But the guy we're playing this week [Dak Prescott] I think is the hardest guy in the league to sack." The cornerback room took some hits with Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) and Jonathan Jones (ankle) getting injured against Pittsburgh. Jones is expected to be sidelined against Dallas, but Fangio indicated Mitchell should be OK to play. Either way, if Philadelphia has any shot of slowing down Dallas, the front seven will have to continue its high level of play. -- Tim McManus

What we're hearing on the Cowboys: The Cowboys are not out of the NFC East picture yet, but they need to keep winning to apply pressure against the Giants. The Cowboys have not posted back-to-back wins since last Thanksgiving, and ex-Cowboys quarterback Joe Milton would love nothing more than to show off against a team that did not believe he was worthy of the backup job to Prescott. But the holiday game has been kind recently to the Cowboys, who have won four in a row. The last time they had a Thanksgiving winning streak that long was from 1980 to 1985. -- Todd Archer

Stat the Eagles are thankful for: In their Week 11 win over the Steelers, running back Saquon Barkley recorded a season-high 61 rushing yards before contact. He also increased his touchdown streak to a career-high four straight games.

Stat the Cowboys are thankful for: Prescott has recorded at least 300 passing yards and five touchdowns in each of his past two games. He is the fourth QB in NFL history to post both of those marks in consecutive games, joining Tom Brady in 2007 (three straight), Ben Roethlisberger in 2014 (two straight) and Daunte Culpepper in 2004 (two straight). -- ESPN Research

Bold prediction: Cowboys DT Quinnen Williams will record multiple sacks for the second straight week. He is scorching hot, with seven sacks in his past six games. When the Cowboys played the Eagles earlier this season, Williams had a sack, recorded a 40% pass rush win rate and notched a 33% pressure rate. -- Walder

Injuries: Eagles | Cowboys

Fantasy nugget: Eagles WR DeVonta Smith returned from a hamstring injury in Week 11 and led the team with 12 targets while playing 81% of the snaps. He finished with only 9.1 fantasy points, but his workload was encouraging. Smith has a favorable matchup against the Cowboys, who are allowing the sixth-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers. See Week 12 rankings. -- Moody

Betting insight: Since coach Brian Schottenheimer was hired in 2025, Dallas games are 21-7 to the over -- the best in the NFL ahead of Baltimore (19-9). Against a potentially injured Eagles secondary, Prescott should be able to easily thread the ball to receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. On the other side, Dallas is allowing 5.2 yards per carry, which could lead to a big game for Barkley. Read more. -- Maldonado

Maldonado's pick: Cowboys 30, Eagles 20

Moody's pick: Cowboys 30, Eagles 17

Walder's pick: Cowboys 31, Eagles 20

FPI prediction: DAL, 82.9% (by an average of 9.4 points)

Thanksgiving game memory for the Eagles: The "Bounty Bowl" in 1989. Rumors swirled heading into the game at Texas Stadium that coach Buddy Ryan had put a $200 bounty on former Eagles kicker Luis Zendejas, who had some critical words aimed at Ryan after leaving the team. That seemed to be confirmed when Eagles linebacker Jessie Small decked Zendejas on a kickoff, leaving the kicker shaken and angered. The game helped fuel one of the fiercest rivalries in football for decades. "I tried to talk to Buddy, but he wouldn't stay on the field. He took his big, fat rear end up the tunnel to the locker room," rookie Cowboys coach Jimmy Johnson said at the time, to which Ryan replied, "I've been on a diet and lost a few pounds. I thought I was looking good and [Johnson] goes and calls me fat. I resent that." -- McManus

Thanksgiving game memory for the Cowboys: Backup quarterback Clint Longley leading the Cowboys to a win over Washington in 1974 is the "best" memory," ruling out Randy Moss' dominant showing in 1998 and Leon Lett's ill-timed trek in the ice in 1993. Longley's comeback vs. Washington came out of nowhere. With Roger Staubach knocked out in the third quarter, the Cowboys trailed 23-17 with less than 30 seconds to play when Longley, known as the "Mad Bomber," hit Drew Pearson for a 50-yard touchdown to defeat their rivals. -- Archer

Matchup must-reads: Eagles' Woolen benched after missed tackles vs. Steelers ... Cowboys need to break a yearlong trend to make the playoffs ... Prescott continues hot streak, salutes Cowboys' offense after rout of Titans

Chiefs (8-2) at Bills (9-1)
Thursday, 8:20 p.m. ET | NBC | BUF -3 (47.5 O/U)

What we're hearing on the Chiefs: The Chiefs didn't celebrate much Sunday following their victory over the Cardinals. They know, after their experience losing to the Cowboys last year on Thanksgiving, that each hour leading up to facing the Bills is critical to their success on the road. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes talked Sunday about when his preparation would begin for the pivotal showdown, which has plenty of implications on the AFC playoff picture. "When I put [my] kids down, then I'll be studying the Buffalo Bills," Mahomes said. -- Nate Taylor

What we're hearing on the Bills: The challenges of facing Josh Allen and Mahomes aren't identical, but Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard -- who spent the past two seasons preparing for Mahomes in Denver -- draws one major comparison: They can beat you even when you're right and they're wrong. The extra wrinkle, of course, is the Chiefs' improved run game. "You take a very highly skilled group of athletes and you've got the trigger man in Mahomes who is able to just disperse the ball all over the place," Leonhard said. "Again, now that they are keeping teams a little bit more honest with the run game, downhill, power and physicality, that makes it even more difficult." -- Nick Suss

Stat the Chiefs are thankful for: If they had scored one more point in Week 11, they would've matched a franchise record of three straight games with 35-plus points. That was last done in 2018, when Mahomes became the Chiefs' starter. However, Kansas City did win its third straight game by 20-plus points, matching a franchise record from 1997.

Stat the Bills are thankful for: They have not allowed a touchdown in three straight games, the longest streak in franchise history. The 43 straight defensive drives without a touchdown is the longest by any team since the 2018-19 Patriots. -- ESPN Research

Bold prediction: Bills TE Dalton Kincaid will score a touchdown. He has only nine receptions over his past three games, but targets against the Chiefs go to tight ends 25% of the time -- the highest rate in the NFL. Kincaid has found the end zone only twice this season. -- Walder

Injuries: Chiefs | Bills

Fantasy nugget: See Week 12 rankings. The Chiefs should lean heavily on running backs Kenneth Walker III and Emmett Johnson against Buffalo. Kansas City's offensive line ranks sixth in run block win rate, and the Bills have allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game to running backs. Buffalo has also surrendered the third-most receptions and receiving yards per game to the position. -- Moody

Betting insight: Bills games have gone under six straight times in November. Kansas City gives up just 3.7 yards per carry, so RB James Cook III might have to grind for his yards. The Chiefs have allowed only eight passing touchdowns, too. I can see both teams settling for field goals here. Read more. -- Maldonado

Maldonado's pick: Chiefs 23, Bills 20

Moody's pick: Bills 27, Chiefs 24

Walder's pick: Bills 28, Chiefs 23

FPI prediction: BUF, 53.1% (by an average of 0.7 points)

Thanksgiving game memory for the Chiefs: Running back Marcus Allen passes Walter Payton in 1996. The Chiefs don't have many fond memories on Thanksgiving, but Allen passed fellow Hall of Famer Payton on the all-time rushing touchdowns list in Detroit. Allen recorded his 111th score on a 1-yard dive into the end zone in the first quarter. His 73 rushing yards and two touchdowns helped the Chiefs rally for a 28-24 comeback victory. The win was sweeter for the Chiefs after their holiday loss a year earlier to the Cowboys. -- Taylor

Thanksgiving game memory for the Bills: Allen's debut on the holiday in 2019. His favorite memory from that game was a mistake. Late in the second quarter, he lined up under center for a fourth-and-1 but fumbled the snap and lost the ball for a good two seconds. Somehow, he found the ball in the mass of humanity in front of him, leaping over the pile and shouldering through former All-Pro linebacker Sean Lee for a first down. "It kind of stinks, though, because if I do my job there it's just an easy handoff to Devin Singletary and he probably walks in for a touchdown," he said. "I had to make it a little harder on ourselves there." The Bills still won 26-15. -- Suss

Matchup must-reads: For Mahomes, don't call it a comeback ... Kelce pads Hall of Fame résumé with two first-half TDs in Chiefs' win ... Brady not satisfied with 9-1 Bills, says team wasn't looking ahead to Chiefs

Previously played

Packers (6-4) at Rams (6-4)
Wednesday, 8 p.m. ET | Netflix | LAR -2.5 (43.5 O/U)

What we're hearing on the Packers: The Packers could start their seventh different offensive line combination in 11 games if veteran guard Kevin Zeitler gets his first start of the season. They had planned to start him last time out against the Vikings until a triceps injury popped up in practice, and the pass protection was worse than it has been all season. The Packers rank last in the NFL in pass block win rate (31%). QB Jordan Love has the shortest time before passing (2.58 seconds) and the second-shortest time to sack (4.12 seconds) this season. And now the Packers have to face Rams defensive linemen Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett. -- Rob Demovsky

What we're hearing on the Rams: For the first time this season, the Rams are expected to have Garrett, Donald, Byron Young and Kobie Turner on the field together. Turner has missed the past four games while on injured reserve because of a groin injury. When asked about the group building chemistry despite a lack of snaps together, Donald said he thinks they're "getting into a rhythm." "I think overall we look pretty damn good in these last two practices we had, playing off each other and communicating," Donald said. "I don't think there are any drop-offs here." -- Sarah Barshop

Stat the Packers are thankful for: Since becoming Packers coach in 2019, Matt LaFleur has dominated his head-to-head meetings against Rams coach Sean McVay. LaFleur is 5-0 against McVay, with the Packers averaging 27.2 points in those wins. LaFleur served as the Rams' OC under McVay in 2017.

Stat the Rams are thankful for: They have won their past four games after starting 2-4, with three of those coming on the road. Their four-game road win streak is behind the Bills (eight) for the second-longest active streak in the NFL. -- ESPN Research

Bold prediction: Rams CB Trent McDuffie will record at least three passes defended. According to my player-tracking data on cornerbacks, McDuffie is playing exceptionally well in coverage this season. NFL Next Gen Stats agrees, ranking him third best among outside corners in yards allowed per coverage snap and second best in percentage of time spent in tight coverage. -- Walder

Injuries: Packers | Rams

Fantasy nugget: Rams running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum face a Packers defense allowing the eighth most fantasy points per game to the position. With Puka Nacua and Davante Adams on injured reserve, Los Angeles should continue to lean on its running game during the final stretch. Both Williams and Corum belong in fantasy lineups this week. See Week 12 rankings. -- Moody

Betting insight: The Rams are 0-10 against the spread and 1-9 outright in their past 10 meetings against the Packers, including the playoffs. With the Rams' struggling passing offense and Green Bay having 14 picks on the season, one short field for Love could make the difference in a close game. Read more. -- Maldonado

Maldonado's pick: Packers 23, Rams 20

Moody's pick: Rams 24, Packers 20

Walder's pick: Packers 21, Rams 17

FPI prediction: LAR, 67.2% (by an average of 4.5 points)

Extra stuffing: Packers' Parsons cleared to make season debut Wednesday ... Why Packers can't protect Love or rush successfully ... Has Nacua played his final snaps in a Rams uniform? ... Rams' Ferguson needs season-ending ankle surgery

Bears (8-2) at Lions (8-2)
Thursday, 1 p.m. ET | CBS | CHI -2.5 (55.5 O/U)

What we're hearing on the Bears: The Bears have not trailed in any of their five straight wins since QB Caleb Williams returned from a hamstring injury. However, the offense grew "stale" late in the past two games after early two-score leads. "There's just something right now that's kind of kept us out of that rhythm of really being able to put our foot on the gas," offensive coordinator Press Taylor said. That can't happen against Detroit's No. 5 scoring offense (28.8 points per game). "It's going to be a shootout," tight end Colston Loveland said. "We know that. We're confident in our guys, though, and confident in our defense, but we know that if it needs to be a 40-40 game or whatever, we can handle that." -- Courtney Cronin

What we're hearing on the Lions: Coach Dan Campbell will welcome his former offensive coordinator, Ben Johnson, back to Detroit with both teams riding at least a five-game win streak. It's the first time that two such teams are facing each other on Thanksgiving, per ESPN Research. The Lions went 2-0 versus the Bears in 2025. "When you're playing pretty good football and you feel like you're getting better, and you feel like you're gaining strength, you almost feel like [the games] can't come fast enough," Campbell said of Detroit's groove. "You're just ready to get to the next one." -- Eric Woodyard

Stat the Bears are thankful for: Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who was acquired from the Titans on Nov. 1, tied a career high with three sacks against the Saints in Week 11. He has had at least one sack in each of his three games since the trade. -- ESPN Research

Stat the Lions are thankful for: They've allowed 21 or fewer points in six straight games, tied for the team's second-longest streak over the past 50 seasons. And Detroit is 5-0 at Ford Field (not including the "home" win over the Patriots in Munich), which is its longest home win streak to start a season since 1991. -- ESPN Research

Bold prediction: Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs will record 6.0 yards per carry. The Bears' defense is already vulnerable against the run, allowing 4.5 yards per carry. But that number climbs up to to 4.9 yards per carry when looking specifically at outside zone runs. The Lions run outside zone 49% of the time, fifth most in the NFL. -- Walder

Injuries: Bears | Lions

Fantasy nugget: Loveland has averaged 7.4 targets and 14.2 fantasy points during Chicago's five-game winning streak. He faces a Lions defense that has allowed the most fantasy points per game to tight ends. Detroit's defense has also allowed the most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks, making it a favorable matchup for Williams. See Week 12 rankings. -- Moody

Betting insight: Goff is 4-0 outright and 3-1 against the spread versus Williams, and Campbell is 2-0 both ways against Johnson. Even if the Bears close up running lanes for Gibbs, Goff can still hit the star running back through the air in space to keep drives moving. Read more. -- Maldonado

Maldonado's pick: Lions 31, Bears 27

Moody's pick: Lions 30, Bears 27

Walder's pick: Bears 31, Lions 24

FPI prediction: DET, 55.3% (by an average of 1.4 points)

Thanksgiving game memory for the Bears: Running back Walter Payton's offensive explosion against the Lions in 1977. The Hall of Famer racked up 244 yards from scrimmage (20 rushes for 137 yards, four catches for 107 yards) and two touchdowns at the Silverdome. The Bears turned the ball over five times, but they pulled off a 31-14 win because of Payton's dominance. The Bears didn't look back after he hauled in a 75-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Bob Avellini in the third quarter. -- Cronin

Thanksgiving game memory for the Lions: Topping the Bears 23-20 in 2024. After three straight Thanksgiving losses as coach of the Lions, Campbell finally ended the team's seven-year drought on the holiday two seasons ago. With the win, the 11-1 Lions also got off to their best start in franchise history. For quarterback Jared Goff, it was a "bucket list" moment, as he enjoyed a turkey leg following his 221 passing yards and two touchdown passes. Goff was in great spirits and joined by teammates David Montgomery, Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, DJ Reader and Al-Quadin Muhammad. -- Woodyard

Matchup must-reads: Simmons matches career high with three sacks in Bears' win ... Bears' Williams has moved on from four-INT game, but frustration lingers ... Lions have best offense in football... Lions' Campbell says Hutchinson injury won't prompt celebration ban

stories.headline: Charles Leclerc urges Ferrari to find 'solution' after clash with Lewis Hamilton
stories.summary: Charles Leclerc has said he and Ferrari teammate Lewis Hamilton must find a "solution" for their run of recent on-track incidents, after admitting it has damaged the atmosphere within the team.
stories.body:
Charles Leclerc has said he and Ferrari teammate Lewis Hamilton must find a "solution" for their run of recent on-track incidents, after admitting it has damaged the atmosphere within the team.

Leclerc collided with Hamilton midway through last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix -- an incident that team principal Fred Vassuer described as "unacceptable."

The clash followed near misses between the Ferrari teammates on the opening laps in Italy and Mexico, the latter of which cost the team a clear shot at victory.

Following the Mexico incident, both drivers claimed talks with Vasseur had helped clear the air, but speaking ahead of this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix, Leclerc admitted a "solution" was still necessary to avoid further clashes.

"I mean, at the end of the day, we are two very strong drivers that want to finish one ahead of the other," Leclerc said. "Unfortunately, it finished recently ... Whether it's in [Las Vegas] or Monza or Mexico, there's been a bit too many events like those lately, and we need to find a solution as a team to make sure that these kind of things don't happen again."

Although he wouldn't give details of what will change within the team, Leclerc said he had clear opinions on how future collisions could be avoided.

"I do have [ideas], and I think I made it very clear," Leclerc said. "But I would rather have these discussions internally.

"And yeah, I do have an opinion, but at the end, what matters is what we think is the right decision collectively, and this will take it internally."

- Haas confirm Ollie Bearman will stay for F1 2027 after 'strange' contract delay

- Qatar Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions

- George Russell breaks silence on Max Verstappen criticism: 'Amusing'

Speaking to Sky Sports on Thursday, Hamilton said he and Leclerc had already spoken about the Las Vegas incident and Ferrari had not yet imposed any strict limitations on how they will go racing.

"We're still free to race, and I think that's the ultimate goal of being here," Hamilton said. "We want to race, right? But of course we don't want what happened last week to ever happen.

"We communicate. Charles and I had a good sit down earlier on and had a chat, and I think moving forwards, I think we're going to be fine. I'm just literally focused on racing hard and fair, and yeah, continue to try and enjoy it.

"We do enjoy racing together, and we do have a really good relationship. It's obviously intense in the background, on the outside it seems a lot more intense than it does on the inside."

Leclerc has been at Ferrari since 2019 and recently signed a long-term agreement committing him to the team beyond the end of the decade.

Hamilton arrived at Ferrari last year off the back of an unprecedented period of success with his former team Mercedes, but the length of the 41-year-old's contract has not been confirmed beyond 2027.

Leclerc insists the two drivers get on with each other off the track but admitted the on-track incidents had damaged the mood within the team.

"We have a very good relationship outside the car with Lewis," he added. "I mean, I wouldn't say the atmosphere is good because obviously we are all disappointed of the situation we find ourselves in, but at the same time we are all grown up and responsible of that, so we've got to find a solution.

"Surely there's not a super happy feeling at the moment. At the same time, I mean, we are the ones that need to find the solutions in order to make that better, so there's also a big willingness in trying to find a solution."

Leclerc stressed that he fully agreed with Vasseur's assessment of the Las Vegas incident and once again accepted the blame.

"I mean, that it is unacceptable, of course," he added. "As a team, we cannot afford to clash between teammates, and I think that is very clear for everyone. For the clash in particular of Las Vegas, as I said, I took responsibility.

"I think there's just tension around that we just need to dissipate and make sure that we look at more positive days in the future. That's all I'm looking for. But yeah, I do agree.

"It's unacceptable that both Ferrari clashes together, of course."

- Williams, Alpine fined £627k by FIA for breaching F1's cost cap

- Min Woo Lee blames F1's Carlos Sainz, Lance Stroll for missing golf club, shoots 68

However, Leclerc said apportioning blame for past incidents was not the same as finding a solution to prevent future collisions.

"I think it's a matter of, at the end of the day, we are two [drivers], one in each car, and we need to make sure that things just work out," he said. "At the moment it's not working, then of course I can take the blame from one episode and whatever, that doesn't really matter.

"Yeah, it's just important that we find a compromise and a solution that works for both. We can discuss about the specific of Las Vegas or somewhere else or the laps before or laps after, but that doesn't really matter. At the end of the day, it's only the solution that matters in that moment. And yeah, that's it."

Leclerc also addressed online rumours that he has a clause in his contract that gives him No.1 status at Ferrari over Hamilton.

"I normally never disclose what I have in my contract, but I think this one is an important one to kind of speak about," he said. "And I absolutely have zero clause that says that in my contract. It's never something that I was interested in and never something that I personally wanted.

"I think the only thing that I don't like seeing is people questioning my integrity to the team, my love for the team. I've been in Ferrari since 2019. I think there's nothing clearer than the love I have for the team. And I'll do absolutely everything in order to bring Ferrari back to the top.

"Then, of course, mistakes happen along the way and always will. We just try to have to minimise them and particularly between teammates. But yeah, I think it's more the question mark of that that I have seen going around that hurts me more than anything else.

"The rest is a lot of noise and it's not the most enjoyable time, but it's part of the game and I have to accept that."

stories.headline: Friday Night Lights,' 'Ted Lasso' top poll ranking 21st-century sports shows
stories.summary: A Seton Hall poll crowns America's favorite modern fictional sports TV series.﻿
stories.body:
It's been quite the year for scripted sports series, with milestones worth celebrating and new chapters worthy of clearing space on the couch.

"Friday Night Lights" hit its two-decade anniversary. "One Tree Hill" turned 23 -- a number Nathan Scott and Michael Jordan would both approve of. On the more modern side, "Ted Lasso" returned for its fourth season, while "All American" wrapped up its Season 8 series finale.

Through different eras and sports, fans have plenty of reasons to get invested, so we tapped Seton Hall for a poll on America's favorite sports show of the 21st century.

"Friday Night Lights" and "Ted Lasso" took the top spots among the general population at 16% and 15%, respectively. The Texas-based football drama also held the edge among avid sports fans, 25% to 22%, and casual sports fans, 23% to 18%.

"The two leaders in the clubhouse for top series indicate that depth and consistency resonate the most with all sports fans," said Len DeLuca, associate director, Seton Hall Sports Poll and instructor in the Seton Hall Stillman Center for sport management. "'Friday Night Lights' was on NBC 14 years before 'Ted Lasso' premiered on Apple TV. This proves that sports content is agnostic to platform."

Whether your loyalty lies with the Dillon Panthers, the Tree Hill Ravens or AFC Richmond, there's a good chance your favorite fictional team has put you through highs and lows. And much like rooting for a real team, picking a favorite show can inspire a spirited debate.

Here are the key findings.

Football leads a multisport lineup
Among the general population, "Friday Night Lights" led all shows at 16%, with "All American" at 10%, "The Game" at 8% and "Ballers" at 7%. That gave football four of the eight highest-polling series overall. Viewers had plenty of interest in the drama surrounding the game, from high school rivalries to the business of professional sports.

Still, football didn't sweep the podium: Soccer's "Ted Lasso" and karate's "Cobra Kai" finished second and third at 15% and 13%, respectively. With 12%, "A League of Their Own" added representation for baseball and took the fourth spot. Hockey's "The Mighty Ducks: Game Changers" and basketball's "One Tree Hill" also drew 7% each, matching "Ballers."

The generation gap
The age ranges didn't differ entirely, but different generations tended to root for different fictional teams.

18-34: "Ted Lasso" led with 17%, followed by "All American," "The Game" and "The English Game" at 14% each. Newer titles also found an audience here: "Heated Rivalry" drew 10%, its strongest showing across the age groups.

35-54: This group showed the most love for "Cobra Kai," which topped its list at 19%. "Friday Night Lights" followed at 18%, with "Ted Lasso" at 15%. "One Tree Hill" and "Eastbound & Down" also had their strongest showings here at 10% each.

55+: "Friday Night Lights" took the lead at 17%, narrowly ahead of "A League of Their Own" at 16%. "Ted Lasso" rounded out the top three at 13%. The drop-off was sharper for teen dramas such as "All American" and "One Tree Hill," which drew 5% and 3%, respectively.

Commonalities and contrasts between sports fans and nonfans
Sports fans and nonfans found some common ground, even if they weren't watching the same shows. "Friday Night Lights" led among sports fans at 23%, followed by "Ted Lasso" at 19% and "Cobra Kai" and "A League of Their Own" at 16% each.

Among nonfans, "Cobra Kai" moved into first at 8%, with "Ted Lasso" and "A League of Their Own" tied at 7%. Coach Eric Taylor (played by Kyle Chandler) had a tougher time with that crowd, as "Friday Night Lights" drew 5%.

The biggest divide, though, was in those who selected "don't know/no opinion": 69% of nonfans compared with 28% of sports fans. The crossover appeal is there, but viewers with less interest in sports need more motivation to tune in.

The men's and women's lineups look a little different
"Friday Night Lights" and "Ted Lasso" finished first and second among both men and women, but the order differs after that. Among men, "Cobra Kai" took third at 15%, followed by "A League of Their Own" at 11%.

Women flipped those two, with "A League of Their Own" drawing 14% and "Cobra Kai" at 11%. "Make It or Break It" and "Heated Rivalry" also drew higher percentages among women than men, both at 6% to 4%.

New shows are earning their stripes
Some newer series are already finding a place alongside the familiar favorites. "Chad Powers" drew 6% overall, followed by "Heated Rivalry" at 5% and "Running Point" and "Off Campus" at 4% each.

For avid sports fans, "Chad Powers" reached 13%, matching "The Game" in that group. "Heated Rivalry," meanwhile, had its strongest showing among adults ages 18-34 at 10%. The established shows have a head start, but the newcomers are getting some playing time.

Editor's Note: These results are derived from a Seton Hall Sports Poll conducted Oct. 8 to Oct. 13, 2026, among 1,632 adults. The Poll, which is sponsored by The Sharkey Institute within Seton Hall University's Stillman School of Business, features a national representative sample from YouGov Plc., weighted on U.S. Census Bureau figures for age, gender, ethnicity, education, income and geography with a margin of error of +/- 3.0 percent.

stories.headline: Cesc Fàbregas plays down Barcelona links, pledges immediate future to Como
stories.summary: Cesc Fabregas has pledged his immediate future to Como amid speculation that he could one day succeed Hansi Flick at Barcelona.
stories.body:
Cesc Fàbregas has pledged his immediate future to Como amid speculation that he could one day succeed Hansi Flick at Barcelona.

The former Arsenal, Barcelona and Chelsea midfielder has attracted the attention of several top clubs after guiding Como to an impressive start in the Champions League -- the Serie A side sit third in the standings, just behind Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain.

Asked about persistent rumours regarding a potential return to Barça after Como's 1-0 victory over AEK Athens on Wednesday, Fabregas told TNT Sports Mexico: "Obviously I'm from there [Barcelona.] I've grown up at that club and I know everyone there, but at the end of the day you have to take each day as it comes.

"Whenever I've tried to look too far ahead, it's never gone well for me. I'm the sort of person who takes each day as it comes.

"In life, we're like pilots flying a plane, and you never know when it's going to slow down. That's why we have to try and enjoy every moment."

Fàbregas, 39, has a contract with Como through June 2028. He reportedly has a clause in his contract that allows him to leave for Barcelona, Chelsea or Arsenal for very little compensation.

"I focus on the day-to-day because thinking about the future normally doesn't take you anywhere," Fàbregas said.

"I try to enjoy it knowing the competitiveness and the demand of being coach of a club like Como that is growing. I have so many responsibilities and I want to keep growing in this club, and above all, in my work."

- Meet Como's Nico Paz, the heir to Lionel Messi's Argentina No. 10 shirt

- Champions League upstarts Como suffer Moise Kean injury blow

Fàbregas played for Como for the 2022-23 season before retiring from football. As interim coach, he steered the club to earn promotion to Italy's top flight in May 2024 -- a third promotion in six seasons for the club.

Como finished fourth in Serie A last season to qualify for the Champions League for the first time in the club's history.

Wednesday's result was Como's fourth win in their opening five games in Europe's elite club competition. Amongst their standout performances include a 4-0 rout of Manchester United and a 9-1 demolition of Lens.

Como face Barcelona on Jan. 27 in the Champions League.

stories.headline: Source: MLS owners agree new 16-team playoff format starting in 2027-28
stories.summary: MLS team owners have agreed on a new playoff format for the 2027-28 season featuring 16 teams, a source confirmed to ESPN.
stories.body:
Major League Soccer's team owners have agreed on a new playoff format for the 2027-28 season, one that will feature 16 teams with two rounds of home-and-home series and single elimination thereafter, a source with knowledge of the league's plans confirmed to ESPN.

The format was approved by team owners at the MLS Board of Governors meeting in Miami on Nov. 12. Aggregate goals will be used to determine the winners in the first two rounds with extra time and penalties used to break ties, though that approach could change, the source said.

The new approach to the postseason will be implemented in conjunction with the league's shift to a summer-to-spring calendar that more closely aligns with leagues in Europe.

The calendar transition will feature what is being called a "sprint season" to take place in the first half of 2027. That competition will feature a 14-game regular season, with the top eight teams from each conference qualifying for the playoffs. Each playoff round in that competition will be single elimination, culminating in MLS Cup on Memorial Day weekend.

The Athletic was the first to report the new playoff format. An official announcement is expected on Dec. 3. The source added that the new format was discussed with broadcast partners and sponsors.

The agreed-upon format for the 2027-28 season reflects a more simplified approach than what was previously being considered.

That previous format would have featured 20 teams in a double elimination system inspired by Australian Rules Football. The number of qualifiers received pushback from fans and media, with the league ultimately agreeing to scale back the number of teams reaching the postseason.

MLS has frequently modified its playoff format over the course of its existence, oscillating between best-of-three and home-and-home series, as well as whether away goals counted as a tiebreaker.

Currently the league uses a system in which 18 teams reach the postseason. A preliminary wild card round involving four teams feeds into a 16-team setup featuring a best-of-three series in the conference quarterfinal round. The conference semifinal, conference final and MLS Cup final are all single elimination.

Part of what drove consideration for the Aussie Rules format was increasing the inventory of playoff games, which typically draw the best ratings. The new format will still contain a total of 27 playoff games. The current approach features between 25 and 33 games. Reducing the number of playoff teams from 18 to 16 will also place more emphasis on the regular season.

The source also confirmed that the 2027-28 regular season will feature a revised format. Teams will be split among five divisions, and will play each of their division rivals twice, and the remainder of the teams in the league once for a total of 34 games.

While the final details still need to be approved, the league is looking at playoff qualification being determined partly by how a team finishes in its division, as well as a league-wide table. Five of the games against division rivals will take place at the end of the season to add some drama to the fight for playoffs places.

stories.headline: Sparks forward Cameron Brink, Ben Felter wed at Stanford
stories.summary: The couple met in 2021 and was engaged in 2024 before marrying at their alma mater's Memorial Church.
stories.body:
Cameron Brink and Ben Felter have officially tied the knot after holding a ceremony on Nov. 14 at their alma mater Stanford's Memorial Church.

According to a report Tuesday from Vogue Magazine, which shared behind-the-scenes details and images, the Los Angeles Sparks forward had four bridal looks, including a custom dress from bridal designer Danielle Frankel for the ceremony, and another for the reception.

Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha, were among those in attendance. Curry and Brink are godsiblings as their fathers were teammates at Virginia Tech, and their mothers were roommates on campus.

The reception was at Ritz-Carlton, Half Moon Bay, while vows were exchanged at Memorial Church, one of the earliest interdenominational churches in the West. The waiting list to get married there can be up to four years, but alumni receive a shorter period, according to Vogue. The couple told the magazine that they always knew they wanted to wed there.

"Walking past the ornate mosaics on my way to class was always the best part of my day," Brink said.

Brink and Felter met at Stanford in the fall of 2020. The two began dating in March 2021 after Felter sent Brink an email in which he included his phone number. Felter, who rowed at Stanford, proposed to Brink in Paris in September 2024.

The No. 2 pick in the 2024 WNBA draft, Brink averaged a career-high 9.5 points plus five rebounds and 1.8 blocks for Los Angeles in the 2026 season.

stories.headline: Price tag for Tassie's new AFL stadium goes up, again
stories.summary: The estimated cost of a new 23,000-seat waterfront venue, set to eventually become the home of the Tasmania Devils, has risen again.
stories.body:
Tasmania's new AFL stadium has suffered another cost blowout, causing the premier to break a promise to cap the state's spend as critics fear the end price will be far higher.

The cost estimate for the 23,000-seat roofed venue at Macquarie Point in Hobart has increased from $1.13 billion to $1.23 billion.

On top of the figure is $132 million for broader precinct infrastructure, project delivery costs of $183 million and unspecified contingencies, taking the total to $1.54 billion.

Premier Jeremy Rockliff previously pledged to cap Tasmania's contribution to the build at $875 million as part of a deal to get the project through parliament.

But he conceded on Tuesday the state would have to cover the slated $100 million increase via extra borrowings.

"The previous cost estimate, which we announced ... some 14 months ago, there's been a lot of water under the bridge since that point," Mr Rockliff said.

The premier confirmed the project wouldn't head back to parliament for the approval of the necessary extra funding, despite previous assurances it would.

The latest estimate reflects increases in the cost of construction, sustained high oil and materials prices, higher labour costs and its complexity, the state government said.

The stadium is expected to be ready for the 2031 AFL season and was a condition of the Tasmania Devils being granted a licence to enter into the national competition in 2028.

It initially had a price tag of $715 million.

Mr Rockliff said the state had reached out to the federal government and AFL for extra money on top of their $240 million and $15 million contributions.

Anti-stadium group Our Place Hobart said the new cost estimate failed to take into account other factors, including the interest bill and the exact cost of contingencies.

Greens leader Rosalie Woodruff described the ongoing cost increases as a deep betrayal of Tasmanians.

"Who knows where the final price for the stadium will end up?" she said.

"What we do know is there's been now a fifth major cost blowout and there's not yet a contract price locked in for this massive project."

Federal independent MP Andrew Wilkie fears the stadium will end up costing $2 billion.

"Once you add the cost of the debt over a decade, the total cost to the Tasmanian taxpayer is closer to $3.5 billion," he said.

Devils chief executive Brendon Gale said the question of any additional funding from the AFL was a matter for the sport's governing body.

"The politicians can politic. We'll get on with building our club," he said.

"People have their views and are entitled to them. But based on my experience, people never look back. These types of projects transform cities and states."

The release of updated costs came ahead of schedule after the government bowed to political pressure to make the figures public before the end of the parliamentary year.

In mid-October, BESIX Watpac was announced as the preferred builder. A final contract is set to be signed by the end of 2026.

BESIX Watpac recently built a 30,000-seat roofed stadium in Christchurch in New Zealand which cost about $540 million.

Mr Rockliff said the final contract price for the Hobart stadium was unlikely to differ from the $1.23 billion estimate.

The stadium has been deeply divisive in Tasmania amid rising state debt, a stretched health system and other under-pressure services.

The AFL and federal government have been contacted for comment.

stories.headline: 'Can't judge them': who Papenhuyzen wants at the Storm
stories.summary: Ex-Melbourne star Ryan Papenhuyzen has made some big calls on who should be the next Storm coach and the one to keep from Cameron Munster and Harry Grant.
stories.body:
Ryan Papenhuyzen empathises with Cameron Munster but believes Melbourne must prioritise keeping Harry Grant if the NRL powerhouse can't hold on to both superstars.

Munster on Tuesday rejected an offer from the Storm believed to be for one year with the option of another season, labelling the terms "disappointing".

The Storm are also fighting to keep Grant, and Papenhuyzen was unequivocal when asked on Wednesday who the club should target if salary-cap pressures meant only one of the newly crowned Australian World Cup winners could stay.

"I went through something similar as Munster where I thought the club had low-balled me," the happily retired 2020 premiership-winning hero told AAP.

"But having my time out of the game now, they've got their reasons for offering those certain amounts and it might not be enough (for Munster).

"Penrith have done it for years and years. They get to a point where they can't hold their players and they've got a price for their players.

"So I understand Munster's perspective. He wants to earn as much as he can in his career and he wants to win a premiership, so that probably limits his opportunities.

"If a club's got money and they're in a premiership window, it's probably a good chance he'll go to that club."

At 28, skipper Grant is four years younger than Munster and more important long-term to the Storm, Papenhuyzen believes.

"Harry's done a brilliant job in terms of leadership," the ex-Clive Churchill Medallist turned caddy said after playing in the Australian PGA Championship pro-am in Sydney.

"The amount of care he has for everyone in that group and the way he thinks about the game, I feel really sorry for him over the last 12 months (when Melbourne missed the finals) because he's always trying to find new ideas to bring everyone.

"He's a great leader for that club going forward. I'd hate to see him go because he's a player you want to build a club around and I guess Munster is towards the back end of his career.

"He had a great World Cup, but World Cups are different to NRL seasons. You've got to lock in for a month with that, and an NRL season's a long time."

Pressed on who he'd keep as a priority, Papenhuyzen said: "Harry's probably the one leadership-wise. Just his qualities are really admirable.

"You know what Munster brings to the game. He gives you confidence standing next to him, knowing what he's going do, but I just think Harry ..."

With coach Craig Bellamy confirming he is moving on at the end of 2027, Papenhuyzen also suspects Grant might be a better for the Storm's new mentor, whomever that may be.

"Harry's really respected and in terms of trying to keep the culture, he's very open-minded too," the BMW golf correspondent said.

"He's open to new ideas, whereas Munster is very much like Bellamy - he's sort of got his way and it's worked for him for so long.

"Whatever they both decide to do, you can't judge them. It's never a right or wrong decision."

Papenhuyzen believes it would be "awesome" if Billy Slater succeeded Bellamy, but suspects "life is too good" for the Storm legend to be a head NRL coach.

"I love Jyles. If he went back there, I'd be awfully encouraged of how well they're going to go. They'd probably be my two."

But Papenhuyzen, also open to helping out the new coach, nominated Bellamy's son Aaron as a left-field option.

"Aaron's awesome with people," he said.

"He's awesome with the wider playing group and he understands that Craig sometimes pushes the boundaries. Aaron's a bit more like Wendy - Craig's, Craig's wife.

"They're both a bit more more gentle, so you've got that loving, nurturing side and potentially (he could do the job).

"I do know you just need people around you. We'd be silly to say the coach controls everything."

stories.headline: George Russell breaks silence on Max Verstappen criticism: 'Amusing'
stories.summary: George Russell has laughed off Max Verstappen's "quite amusing" put-down of him in Las Vegas, saying he is ready to move on from the latest exchange in their long-running feud.
stories.body:
George Russell has laughed off Max Verstappen's "quite amusing" put-down of him in Las Vegas, saying he is ready to move on from the latest exchange in their long-running feud.

After winning last week's Las Vegas Grand Prix, Verstappen derided Russell's 2026 season as a "complete joke" and said the Englishman was "so far below my level" that he was unbothered by criticism made earlier in the weekend.

Verstappen also mocked the mistake Russell made while fighting Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli, which dropped him from third to ninth.

Speaking in a news conference on Thursday ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix, Russell seemed unbothered by the comments.

"I don't really have much to say to be honest. It was quite amusing," Russell said.

"I found some of the comments post-race, but, you know, at the end of the day, he drove an incredible race and won it. So he can afford to say what he wants, really. And from my side, yeah, moving on."

Russell had criticised Verstappen after qualifying in Las Vegas for an incident between them during the final practice session earlier that day.

Russell, who has spoken out about Verstappen previously, said "somebody needs to stand up to that guy" and that the four-time world champion walks around like he is "bigger and better" than all his rivals.

Verstappen referenced those comments after his win in Vegas, telling Dutch broadcaster ViaPlay: "His comments don't motivate me, because he's nowhere near me. All talk off the track and a complete joke on it this season. [His mistake was] Perfect Karma."

Russell declined the opportunity to say anything in reply.

Asked if he had anything to say back, he said on Thursday: "No, not really, to be honest, not really. It's, you know, at the end of the day, I guess I stand by what I said after practice, but he was the one who went out and won the race. I didn't. I'm sure he had a bit of a laugh about that. And that was reasonably amusing. So yeah, from my side, just new race weekend, try and focus on the driving and move on."

Verstappen's comments became the biggest talking point out of the Las Vegas race.

- Qatar Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions

- Haas confirm Ollie Bearman will stay for F1 2027 after 'strange' contract delay

- Williams, Alpine fined £627k by FIA for breaching F1's cost cap

Russell believes his good relationship with the media has been a double-edged sword for him in terms of Verstappen and things he has said previously.

"I think I maybe have been guilty of being just too open and honest when I speak with you guys," he said. "You know, I feel with all of the media and the journalists I have a good relationship with. And you sometimes forget that you're not talking to one person.

"You know, we're having a conversation now and you forget, actually, I'm not really talking to you. I'm talking to millions of people on the television. So I think that good relationship has actually probably hindered me a little bit.

"And that's, I guess, life lessons in this world we live. But there's no, you know, the competition is on track. And I think that's where I want to have the battles.

"That's where I want to have the fights. I respect Max immensely for his driving talents and everything he's achieved on track. And that's that, really."

A lot has been made of Russell and Verstappen's back and forth.

The setting of Russell's news conference was ironic as it was in Qatar that their feud exploded into the public eye two years ago. At the 2024 race, Verstappen was given a one-place grid penalty after the stewards deemed he had driven unnecessarily slowly on a preparation lap in qualifying, which Russell had seemingly needed to take evasive action to avoid.

Verstappen was irate with the Mercedes driver, who he felt had lobbied for him to get the penalty in the stewards room.

At media day for the following race in Abu Dhabi, Russell said Verstappen had threatened to put his "f-----g head in the wall" the next time they were on track together.

He also gave a much-quoted interview on TV, where he said: "Whenever anything is not going his way, [Verstappen] lashes out with unnecessary anger and borderline violence. We've seen it in Brazil in the past with [Esteban] Ocon, we saw it in '21 with Lewis [Hamilton], in Mexico with Lando [Norris], in Budapest when he didn't have the most dominant car, crashes into Lewis, slamming his whole team. That is not a guy who I respect, and I wish he would be a better role model."

Broadcasters such as Sky Sports F1's Ted Kravitz and Will Buxton, formerly of F1 TV, have both since suggested Russell sought them out and specifically asked them to ask about Verstappen.

Addressing that famous soundbite on Thursday, Russell suggested he saw it differently.

"I remember in Abu Dhabi a few years ago when I was having, like, an open conversation with Ted Kravitz and Will Burton [Buxton] about the whole situation.

"And I said, well, just ask me the question on camera rather than having the conversation off camera. So they asked me the question on camera, and then go away and they spin the truth into something slightly different. So you kind of think like that's a little bit cheeky because it is the truth, but it's not how it was in reality.

"So, as I said, that's just the learning for me personally."
